To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 20Z and 20E stereoisomers of MIVE exhibit similar biodistribution, metabolism and dosimetry.

the biodistribution of 20E and (20Z)-iodovinylestrogens in healthy women and in breast cancer patients is similar and that (20Z)-MIVE uptake in breast cancer patients correlates with the presence of estrogen receptor.

20E- and 20Z-[123I]MVE have similar biodistribution and radiation dosimetry, (20Z)-MIVE has a high tumor-to-background ratio in estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, and (20Z)-123IMVE has a high tumor uptake in breast cancer patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of radioligands for the diagnosis and therapy of estrogen-dependent tumors.
the development of new radiopharmaceutical for the diagnosis and therapy of breast cancer.
the development and evaluation of a radiopharmaceutical for the imaging of estrogen receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
(20Z)-MIVE is a promising radiopharmaceutical for breast cancer diagnosis and imaging.
(20E)-[123I]-MIVE is the radiopharmaceutical of choice for imaging estrogen receptor-positive tumors.
the 20Z stereospecific isomer of (17alpha)-[123I]-iodovinylestrogen is a promising radiotracer for the diagnosis of breast cancer and for monitoring the response of the tumor to hormonal therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 11 beta-methyl group is not essential for the binding of 20E and (20Z)-iodovinylesteradiol to ERs.
the 20Z stereomer of MIVE is the best of all the radiotracers we have developed for imaging ER-positive tumors.
(20Z)-iodovinyl-11 beta-methoxyl estradiol is a promising radiotracer for the diagnosis of breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
(20Z)-MIVE is a promising radiopharmaceutical for imaging of estrogen receptor-positive cancers.
the 20Z stereosomer is stable and can be used for clinical studies in women with breast cancer.
the 20Z and 20E isomers exhibit similar pharmacokinetic and dosimetric profiles.
